physics_goals.quote: The NuTeV collaboration has extracted sin^2theta_W from the ratios of neutral current to charged current neutrino and anti-neutrino cross-sections.
physics_goals.value: Measure the weak mixing angle sin^2(theta_W) and other electroweak parameters precisely from neutral-current to charged-current neutrino and antineutrino cross-section ratios

summary.plain: A Fermilab experiment in 1996-97 that fired separate beams of almost pure neutrinos and antineutrinos at a 690-tonne detector to measure the weak mixing angle precisely. Its value came out three standard deviations away from the Standard Model prediction, a puzzle still discussed.
summary.technical: Fermilab E815: sign-selected quadrupole-train beams of nu_mu and anti-nu_mu from 800 GeV protons on BeO, detected 1450 m downstream in the 690 t steel-scintillator target calorimeter plus toroid spectrometer. The NC/CC cross-section ratios gave sin^2(theta_W)(on-shell) = 0.2277 +- 0.0013 (stat) +- 0.0009 (syst), 3 sigma above the Standard Model (PRL 88, 091802).
